violations.description: Dangerous pull_request_target workflow checks out untrusted PR head code and runs with write-all permissions and secret access.
violations.evidence: .github/workflows/preview.yml uses pull_request_target, checks out ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}, sets permissions: write-all, and exposes secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN.
violations.recommendation: Replace pull_request_target with pull_request, remove write-all permissions, and do not pass deployment secrets to PR preview builds.

violations.description: CI workflow triggers on master branch but repository default branch is main.
violations.recommendation: Update CI workflow triggers to target main instead of master.

violations.description: Overly broad GITHUB_TOKEN permissions (write-all) configured in PR preview workflow.
violations.recommendation: Set explicit, least-privilege permissions (e.g. contents: read) instead of write-all.

violations.description: Untrusted GitHub event data interpolated directly into shell command in workflow.
violations.evidence: run: echo "Building preview for ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" in .github/workflows/preview.yml line 17.
violations.recommendation: Pass the pull request title via an environment variable rather than direct string interpolation in shell scripts.

violations.description: A live-looking deployment token was committed in git history (scripts/deploy.sh in commit 26b5a8f).
violations.evidence: scripts/deploy.sh added in commit 26b5a8f with DEPLOY_TOKEN=[REDACTED:len=28] (removed in subsequent commit 1f3d3f5).
violations.recommendation: Revoke the leaked DEPLOY_TOKEN immediately and purge git history using git-filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner.

violations.description: Machine-specific absolute Windows paths hardcoded in settings and IDE configuration.
violations.evidence: DATA_DIR = "C:/Users/jdoe/projects/metrics/data" in metrics/settings.py line 5 and "python.defaultInterpreterPath": "C:\\Users\\jdoe\\envs\\metrics\\python.exe" in .vscode/settings.json line 2.
violations.recommendation: Use portable paths relative to the project root or environment variables instead of hardcoded user-specific Windows paths.

violations.description: Inconsistent dependency specifications across pyproject.toml and requirements.txt.
violations.evidence: pyproject.toml specifies requests>=2.20,<2.30 while requirements.txt pins requests==2.31.0 and adds uvicorn==0.29.0.
violations.recommendation: Consolidate dependency declarations so pyproject.toml and requirements.txt are consistent.

violations.description: Test failures are masked in CI using || true.
violations.recommendation: Remove || true so that test failures correctly fail the CI pipeline.
